title: Slippe å eller la være å — need not or choose not to
goal: Distinguish an externally removed requirement from intentional non-action.

objectives.statement: Distinguish an externally removed requirement from intentional non-action.

spans.value: Nora and Emil are helping at a neighborhood event on Saturday. The organizer, Sigrid, has sent them an update.
Har du fått melding fra Sigrid?

blocks.translation: Have you received a message from Sigrid?

spans.value: Ja. Vi slipper å møte klokka sju. Vaktmesteren åpner lokalet for oss.

blocks.translation: Yes. We don’t have to meet at seven. The caretaker will open the venue for us.

spans.value: Så bra. Og vi slipper å bære bordene, fordi de blir levert.

blocks.translation: That’s good. And we don’t have to carry the tables because they’re being delivered.

spans.value: Nettopp. Men jeg lar være å sykle dit. Det skal visst bli veldig glatt.

blocks.translation: Exactly. But I’m choosing not to cycle there. Apparently, it’s going to be very icy.

spans.value: Har Sigrid sagt at du ikke kan sykle?

blocks.translation: Has Sigrid said that you can’t cycle?

spans.value: Nei, det er mitt eget valg. Jeg tar bussen.

blocks.translation: No, it’s my own choice. I’ll take the bus.

spans.value: Jeg skulle egentlig bake to kaker, men Sigrid har bestilt kaker fra et bakeri.

blocks.translation: I was actually going to bake two cakes, but Sigrid has ordered cakes from a bakery.
Then you don’t have to bake.

spans.value: Ja. Men jeg lar være å kjøpe mer kaffe. Vi har allerede nok.

blocks.translation: Yes. But I’ll refrain from buying more coffee. We already have enough.

spans.value: Several planned actions are no longer required, while two other actions will not happen by personal choice. Nora and Emil no longer need to arrive early, carry tables, or bake because someone else has made arrangements. By contrast, Emil personally decides not to cycle, and Nora personally decides not to buy more coffee.

sections.title: When a requirement disappears: slippe å

spans.value: when an action is not necessary or someone is spared a requirement, task, or burden. In the situations practiced here, another person, a rule, an arrangement, or the circumstances remove the need.
. Depending on context, it can also mean

no.value: Vi slipper å møte klokka sju.

en.value: We don’t have to meet at seven.

spans.value: The original plan required an early meeting. The caretaker’s help removes that requirement.

no.value: Nora slipper å bake kakene.

en.value: Nora doesn’t have to bake the cakes.

spans.value: The bakery order means that baking is no longer necessary.

no.value: Du slipper å betale for billetten.

en.value: You don’t have to pay for the ticket.

spans.value: Someone else may be paying, or the ticket may be free. The important point is that payment is not required from you.

no.value: Elevene slipper å ta prøven på nytt.

en.value: The pupils don’t have to take the test again.

spans.value: A teacher or another circumstance has removed the requirement.

no.value: På grunn av regnet slapp vi å vanne hagen.

en.value: Because of the rain, we didn’t have to water the garden.

spans.value: Here, weather—not a personal decision—made the task unnecessary.

In this lesson’s requirement and task examples, the expression tells us that the action is not necessary. That lack of obligation alone does not determine whether the optional action occurs. In the following example, the speaker may still decide to call, but that possibility comes from the context rather than from

no.value: Jeg slipper å ringe henne, men jeg gjør det kanskje likevel.

en.value: I don’t have to call her, but I may do it anyway.

spans.value: Return to Nora and Emil’s conversation. Identify each use of
and state what removed the requirement: the caretaker, the delivery, or the bakery order.

This activity belongs here because these dialogue examples contrast arrangements that remove requirements with personal choices not to act. A successful response would connect each task that is no longer required to the arrangement described in the dialogue rather than claim that Nora or Emil necessarily does not perform it.

sections.title: When someone intentionally does nothing: la være å

spans.value: when a person deliberately refrains from an action. The action is possible, but the person chooses not to do it.

no.value: Emil lar være å sykle fordi veien er glatt.

en.value: Emil chooses not to cycle because the road is icy.

spans.value: Nobody has removed a cycling requirement. Cycling was an available option, and Emil rejects it.

no.value: Nora lar være å kjøpe mer kaffe.

en.value: Nora refrains from buying more coffee.

spans.value: She could buy coffee, but she decides that it is unnecessary.

no.value: Jeg lar være å svare når jeg er sint.

en.value: I refrain from replying when I’m angry.

spans.value: The speaker deliberately waits instead of responding.

no.value: Han lot være å kommentere feilen.

en.value: He chose not to comment on the mistake.

spans.value: He had an opportunity to comment but intentionally remained silent.

no.value: Vi lot være å bestille dessert.

en.value: We decided not to order dessert.

spans.value: Ordering dessert was possible, but the group chose not to do it.
Look again at Emil’s decision about cycling and Nora’s decision about coffee. Explain what each person could have done and why the final non-action counts as a choice.

This checkpoint makes the contrast visible before you begin producing the expressions yourself. A successful response would mention that the actions remain possible and that Emil or Nora intentionally rejects them.
Compare the two expressions with exactly the same action:

no.value: Jeg slipper å kjøre til jobb i morgen.

en.value: I don’t have to drive to work tomorrow.

spans.value: Perhaps a colleague will collect the speaker, or the speaker can work from home. An external arrangement has removed the need to drive.

no.value: Jeg lar være å kjøre til jobb i morgen.

en.value: I’m choosing not to drive to work tomorrow.

spans.value: Driving is still an option, but the speaker has decided against it.

no.value: Sara slipper å lage middag.

en.value: Sara doesn’t have to make dinner.

spans.value: Someone else is cooking, or dinner has already been prepared.

no.value: Sara lar være å lage middag.

en.value: Sara chooses not to make dinner.

spans.value: Sara intentionally does not cook. Without more context, listeners may wonder what she plans to eat instead.

no.value: Vi slipper å sende inn skjemaet.

en.value: We don’t have to submit the form.

no.value: Vi lar være å sende inn skjemaet.

en.value: We choose not to submit the form.

spans.value: Submitting it is possible, perhaps even expected, but the group deliberately refrains.
A quick question can guide your choice in the situations practiced here:

items.value: Is the action no longer necessary, as in this lesson’s arrangement-based examples? Use
Did someone intentionally refrain from an available action? Use

no.value: Hun slipper å vente.

en.value: She doesn’t have to wait.

no.value: Hun lar være å vente.

en.value: She chooses not to wait.

spans.value: . For recognition, you may also encounter the past forms

no.value: I går slapp jeg å jobbe overtid.

en.value: Yesterday I didn’t have to work overtime.

no.value: I går lot jeg være å svare på meldingen.

en.value: Yesterday I chose not to reply to the message.

sections.title: What the two expressions do not mean

spans.value: In this lesson’s requirement and task examples, slippe å does not guarantee non-action

no.value: Jeg slipper å delta på møtet.

en.value: I don’t have to attend the meeting.

spans.value: This does not necessarily mean that the speaker will stay away. Attendance is optional.
If the speaker has made a deliberate decision not to attend,

no.value: Jeg lar være å delta på møtet.

en.value: I’m choosing not to attend the meeting.

spans.value: La være å does not remove a requirement
Suppose a manager says that a report is no longer necessary.

no.value: Du slipper å skrive rapporten.

en.value: You don’t have to write the report.

spans.value: would shift the meaning toward deliberate non-action:

no.value: Hun lar være å skrive rapporten.

en.value: She chooses not to write the report.

spans.value: This describes a person who intentionally does not write it; it does not make a claim about whether writing remains possible or expected.

no.value: Vi slipper å rydde.

en.value: We don’t have to tidy up.

no.value: Vi lar være å rydde.

en.value: We choose not to tidy up.

spans.value: Consider pairs about everyday tasks such as paying a fee, attending a meeting, cooking dinner, taking a bus, or answering a message. For each pair, use the supplied context to explain which sentence says the task is not required because of an external event and which presents intentional non-action. Add one plausible reason for each interpretation.
This activity develops meaning rather than mechanical substitution. In this bounded practice, a successful response would connect the
sentence to the supplied waiver or arrangement and the
sentence to an intentional choice instead of translating both as a general negative.

For example, a fee might be waived by an organizer, while a person might deliberately refrain from paying because they dispute it. Those situations are not interchangeable, even though payment does not occur in either one.

sections.title: Practice: build a cause before choosing the phrase

spans.value: Create short two-sentence situations. In the first sentence, establish either an outside arrangement or a personal decision. In the second, summarize the result with

items.value: a colleague taking over a work task;
bad weather influencing a travel decision;
someone deciding not to send an angry message;
someone avoiding sweets for the day.

spans.value: Do not choose the expression until the assigned context is clear. In these practice situations, a successful response would make the second sentence express either the absent necessity or the deliberate choice established by the first.
On Friday evening, Sigrid sends another message.
Lokalet er allerede pyntet, så dere slipper å komme tidlig.

blocks.translation: The venue has already been decorated, so you don’t have to come early.

spans.value: Flott. Da lar jeg være å sette alarmen på seks.

blocks.translation: Great. Then I won’t set the alarm for six.

spans.value: Jeg slipper også å hente kakene. Bakeriet kjører dem ut.

blocks.translation: I also don’t have to collect the cakes. The bakery is delivering them.

spans.value: Skal du kjøpe blomster på veien?

blocks.translation: Are you going to buy flowers on the way?

spans.value: Nei, jeg lar være. Vi har nok pynt allerede.

blocks.translation: No, I won’t. We already have enough decorations.

spans.value: Notice how this event supports both meanings in the dialogue. Because the venue is ready, Emil does not need to arrive early. He then personally decides not to set an early alarm. Similarly, Nora does not need to collect the cakes because of the delivery, while her decision about flowers remains her own.

Continue the preparations with several short updates. Include at least one task removed by Sigrid, a delivery service, the weather, or another arrangement, and at least one action that Nora or Emil deliberately decides not to perform.

Without looking back, complete these two ideas in Norwegian and briefly explain the difference:

items.value: Something changed, so you no longer need to do a task.
The task remains possible, but you deliberately choose not to do it.

prompt.value: Use the Saturday-event context. The three relevant tasks are meeting early, collecting the cakes, and baking the cakes. Choose the complete interpretation that connects each task to the caretaker, the delivery, or the bakery order. The interpretation must show that slippe å removes a requirement, not that the task is necessarily not performed.

options.text: Vaktmesterens hjelp gjør at vi slipper å møte tidlig; leveringen gjør at Nora slipper å hente kakene; bestillingen hos bakeriet gjør at Nora slipper å bake kakene. Kravene er fjernet, men setningene sier ikke at oppgavene ikke blir gjort.
options.why: The caretaker removes the need to meet early, the delivery removes the need to collect the cakes, and the bakery order removes the need to bake them. None of this proves that the actions do not happen.

options.text: Vaktmesterens hjelp gjør at vi slipper å bake kakene; leveringen gjør at Nora slipper å møte tidlig; bestillingen hos bakeriet gjør at Nora slipper å hente kakene. Ordningene er eksterne, men koblingene er feil.
options.why: The arrangements are assigned to the wrong tasks.

options.text: Vaktmesterens hjelp gjør at vi lar være å møte tidlig; leveringen gjør at Nora lar være å hente kakene; bestillingen hos bakeriet gjør at Nora lar være å bake kakene. Alle tre oppgavene er fortsatt mulige, men dette er personlige valg.
options.why: The context describes requirements removed by arrangements, not deliberate personal decisions.

stem.value: Which interpretation correctly connects the three uses of slippe å to the arrangements?

prompt.value: Use the examples about Emil cycling and Nora buying more coffee. Choose the interpretation that explains both decisions, including that each action remains possible and is deliberately rejected.

options.text: Emil slipper å sykle fordi veien er glatt, og Nora slipper å kjøpe mer kaffe. Handlingene er derfor bare unødvendige, ikke bevisste valg.
options.why: This treats both situations as absent necessity instead of deliberate non-action.

options.text: Emil kunne sykle, men veien gjør sykling umulig; Nora kunne kjøpe mer kaffe, men en regel gjør kjøpet umulig. De lar være å handle fordi handlingene ikke lenger er mulige.
options.why: The lesson says the actions remain available; the people choose not to do them.

options.text: Emil kunne sykle, men han lar være å sykle fordi veien er glatt. Nora kunne kjøpe mer kaffe, men hun lar være å kjøpe mer kaffe fordi hun bestemmer seg for ikke å gjøre det.
options.why: Both actions remain possible, and each person deliberately chooses not to perform the action.

prompt.value: Read the paired situations below. In Norwegian, explain which sentence expresses absent necessity caused by an external arrangement and which expresses deliberate non-action. Add one plausible reason for each interpretation. Do not translate both expressions as a general negative. - Arrangøren dekker gebyret for Ida. Ida slipper å betale gebyret. - Jonas kan svare på meldingen, men han lar være å svare på meldingen.

prompt.value: Write two separate two-sentence situations in Norwegian. In the first, sentence 1 must establish that a colleague takes over a work task, and sentence 2 must summarize the result with slipper å. In the second, sentence 1 must establish that you decide not to send an angry message, and sentence 2 must summarize the result with lar være å. Put each cause or decision before its phrase, and do not use either target expression until sentence 2 of its situation.

criteria.instruction: Establishes the colleague's takeover in sentence 1 and uses slipper å in sentence 2 to express absent necessity.
Establishes the decision not to send an angry message in sentence 1 and uses lar være å in sentence 2 to express deliberate non-action.

prompt.value: Continue this Saturday preparation exchange in Norwegian with 3–5 short updates involving Sigrid, Nora, and Emil. Do not copy the given lines. Sigrid: Lokalet er allerede pyntet, så dere slipper å komme tidlig. Emil: Flott. Da lar jeg være å sette alarmen på seks. Nora: Jeg slipper også å hente kakene. Bakeriet kjører dem ut. Include at least one new task that is no longer required because of Sigrid, a delivery service, the weather, or another arrangement. Use slippe å and state the arrangement that explains it. Also include at least one action that Nora or Emil deliberately chooses not to perform, using la være å.

criteria.instruction: Uses a natural form of slippe å for a newly described task that is no longer required and explicitly includes the arrangement that removed the need.
Uses a natural form of la være å for an action Nora or Emil intentionally chooses not to perform.

prompt.value: Write both final-review ideas in Norwegian and briefly explain the difference. For the first idea, describe a changed situation that removes the need to do a task and use the present frame slipper å. For the second, describe a task that remains possible but is deliberately not done and use the present frame lar være å. Use your own tasks rather than copying a complete prompt sentence, then add one brief Norwegian explanation of the contrast.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian review against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål paraphrases that preserve the two meanings.

criteria.instruction: Uses slipper å for the first idea, where a changed situation removes the need to perform the task.
Uses lar være å for the second idea, where the task remains possible but is deliberately not performed.
Briefly explains in Norwegian the difference between absent necessity and intentional non-action.
